html:
The Aztec Empire was an alliance of three Nahua city-states in the Valley of Mexico: Mexico-Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan. It ruled most of central Mexico from 1428 until Spanish forces and their Indigenous allies destroyed it in 1521.

The Mexica had arrived in the valley as latecomers and founded Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco around 1325 (see Tenochtitlan founded). For a century they served the stronger city of Azcapotzalco. In 1428 they joined Texcoco and Tlacopan to overthrow it, and the winners formed the alliance. Over time Tenochtitlan became the dominant partner. Texcoco, under its poet-king Nezahualcoyotl, was known for law and learning.

Aztec rule was indirect. Conquered cities kept their own rulers as long as they paid tribute: maize, cotton cloth, cacao, feathers, gold and warriors. Wars also supplied captives for human sacrifice to gods such as Huitzilopochtli, the god of war and the sun. Tenochtitlan grew into a city of perhaps 200,000 people, with causeways, canals, floating gardens and the Templo Mayor at its centre.

The empire had many enemies, above all Tlaxcala, which it never conquered. When Hernán Cortés landed in 1519, tens of thousands of Tlaxcalans and other subject peoples joined him. With Moctezuma II dead and smallpox killing many in the city, Tenochtitlan fell in 1521 (see Fall of Tenochtitlan). Mexico City was built on its ruins, and Nahuatl is still spoken by more than a million people.
sum: The Aztec Empire was an alliance of three Nahua city-states in the Valley of Mexico: Mexico-Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan. It ruled most of central Mexico from 1428 until Spanish forces and their Indigenous allies destroyed it in 1521.
